original_test_intent: Read each installed CPU's maximum supported power-capping value from the intended BMC interface, map every response field to the correct CPU and units, and compare it to an authoritative platform baseline without altering power policy.
original_method: Master specifies OEM 0x30/0x26 plus Ethernet Interface Select. Review preserves that method and requires firmware-matched selector and response schema; it rejects selector-less or setter substitutions.
manual_activity: Owner/vendor confirms command applicability, interface selector, per-CPU field order/units and the accepted maximum-power baseline; the resulting read can then run unattended without mutation approval.
required_inputs: Installed CPU topology and stable socket identity
Response length and per-CPU field layout
Approved maximum value per CPU or SPEC tolerance
safety_requirements: Do not omit or guess interface selector
Do not use sshpass or disable host-key verification
Validate target and CPU topology before query
Validate completion and full response length
Decode each CPU field with documented units
Do not issue a setter or change power policy to resolve mismatch
agent_execution_scope: Build one protected 0x30/0x26 request with validated selector
Map each field to physical CPU/socket identity
Decode value, scale, units and sentinel state
Return redacted raw and structured evidence
Prove no policy or platform state changed
engineer_actions: Define expected maximum values and tolerance
Resolve unsupported or contradictory results and own final DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not fit: it omits the required selector, uses insecure SSH, offers irrelevant LAN evidence and mischaracterizes the read as a state-changing operation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x26 <validated-Ethernet-Interface-Select>` only with the firmware-matched response parser; never invoke a setter from this case.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact 0x30/0x26 family, selector placeholder and 10/5 timing remain unchanged; no selector, CPU count, units or values are guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the OEM query to the documented BMC interface and live CPU topology, decode every per-CPU maximum using the vendor schema, then compare to a project-approved baseline while recording non-mutation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target identity, structured decoding, units, topology mapping and secure access while preserving the read-only source purpose.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A selector-less raw response or generic LAN output cannot prove which interface/CPU each maximum belongs to; a setter would be different and unauthorized coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong field order, units or CPU topology can produce plausible but incorrect maximum values and misstate platform power capability.

project_override_considerations: A vendor utility or API is equivalent only if it returns the same per-CPU maximum semantics with socket identity and units and records whether raw 0x30/0x26 remains untested.
expected_evidence: CPU topology and stable socket ordering
Redacted exact request and raw response
Per-CPU decoded maxima, scale and units
Approved baseline/tolerance comparison or readiness-pending note

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Get title and criteria define a read-only per-CPU maximum query, but DeepSeek/source risk labels it a write, omits the source's interface selector and uses insecure access plus unrelated verification. Review resolves recommendation semantics without altering Master.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read objective is clear. Selector, response schema, topology and expected values are vendor/project execution inputs, so review can complete without a permanent block or unsafe mutation.

review_improvement: Separates the read from any setter, requires selector-aware OEM decoding and CPU topology mapping, and replaces transport success with per-socket value/units evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A list of numeric bytes is insufficient for power-capping capability: socket order, value width, scale, units and sentinel meanings are firmware-defined. Since the title and expected result expressly request maximum values, no state change is needed. The main engineering risk is false attribution, so the evidence must tie the selector and response fields to the actual CPU topology rather than treating command completion as PASS.
